scenes.narration: When global stock markets drop thirty percent in a single quarter, retail investors rush toward cash. Yet at that exact moment, the world's largest sovereign wealth funds begin buying billions of dollars in discounted equities using a strict mathematical rulebook.

Managing over one point six trillion dollars across nine thousand companies, Norway's Government Pension Fund Global enforces a rigid seventy-to-thirty split between global stocks and government bonds. Whenever equities fall sharply, the fund automatically sells bonds and buys stocks to restore its target ratio.

This counter-cyclical rebalancing forces the institution to buy low during recessions and trim high during euphoric bull markets without relying on human market timing. Over three decades, that single mechanical discipline has added tens of billions in compounding excess returns.
